text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovak opposition parties, with the exception of the Party of Democratic Left (SDL), will start collecting signatures on Thursday for a petition to initiate a referendum on the direct election of the president.

- Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik said his German counterpart Klaus Kinkel is expected to visit Slovakia in the near future. Hamzik said Germany had also expressed interest in a visit of Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The European Investment Bank (EIB) extended loans worth 353 million ECU in Slovakia last year, compared with 832 million ECU in Hungary and 737 million ECU in the Czech Republic.
- The abolition of the import surcharge at the beginning of this year is not likely to lead to a decrease in retail prices.

- The Statistical Bureau said that, according to preliminary figures, industrial production decreased last December. But most of the companies included in the survey said that they expected to increase production in the first months of this year.

- The largest producer of hygienic paper, PT Zilina, expects turnover of around 2.5 billion crowns this year. The company said that about 90 percent of its production will be exported to Czech Republic, Italy, Germany, Austria and Britain.

PRAVDA - Peter Magvasi of the opposition SDL accused SAS, the majority owner of the heavy engineering company Povazske Strojarne, of chanelling funds from a bond issue to its own account and using the money to repay loans drawn to acquire control over the company.
- The trade union of medical doctors warned that if the goverment fails to fulfil its promise of a 35 percent pay rise this month, doctors will start a protest strike in February.
